# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 65 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | Coptic

---

## Saying 65

He said: "A good man had a vineyard. He leased it to some farmers so that they would work it and he would receive the produce from them. He sent his servant so that the farmers would give him the produce of the vineyard. They seized his servant and beat him — all but killing him. The servant went and told his master. The master said: 'Perhaps he did not know them.' He sent another servant. The farmers beat that one as well. Then the master sent his son and said: 'Perhaps they will respect my son.' Because the farmers knew that he was the heir to the vineyard, they seized him and killed him. Whoever has ears, let him hear."

---

**Translator's Notes (EMET):**

- Parallel to Mark 12:1-9, Matthew 21:33-41, Luke 20:9-16; Thomas version is shorter and lacks allegorical clues
- Thomas omits the Isaiah 5 vineyard quote that frames Mark's version
- "A good man" — Thomas adds *agathos* qualifier absent from Synoptics
- The master's double rationalization ("Perhaps he did not know them... Perhaps they will respect my son") gives a more naive, human portrait than the Synoptic owner
- No divine judgment at the end; the saying ends with the death and the hearing formula
